entries.claim: Defined sample: the 40 most recent English-language Trustpilot reviews of ai.invideo.io (sort=recency, pages 1-2, posted 2026-09-08 to 2026-11-20) split 31 one-star, 1 two-star, 1 three-star, 1 four-star, 6 five-star. 21 of 40 describe credits running out fast, more credits being demanded mid-video or unexpected credit use; 7 of those 21 say credits went on the AI's own errors, retries, loops or fixes. At least 6 of 40 describe billing or refund disputes; themes are multi-label, so the sub-codes overlap: at least 4 refused or unanswered refunds, 2 unintended annual charges, 2 automatic credit top-up charges, 1 billing after cancelling. At least 6 of 40 criticise output quality or prompt-following; 3 of 40 say the free tier ends before anything usable; 3 of 40 describe slow rendering. 4 of 40 praise support; 5 of the 6 five-star reviews came through Trustpilot's invitation link (BasicLink).
entries.quote: Before it was even finished, I was told I had run out of credits and needed to pay MORE!
entries.platform: Trustpilot trustpilot.com/review/ai.invideo.io (review platform, claimed profile; read live 2026-11-20 via built-in browser, page JSON)

entries.quote_supplementary: Quote is from review 6aec2ac6863d6198208937ab (2026-11-05, 1 star, KR). Coded review ids, stars and resolved theme codes are in _meta.trustpilot_sample.
honesty_notes: Themes are multi-label; counts do not sum to 40, and the billing sub-codes (4+2+2+1) exceed the parent 6 because one review can carry several. 3 of 40 had no codable detail ('SCAM Be Careful', 'Scam don't waste...', a one-line Spanish review under the English filter).

Complaint bias: Trustpilot over-represents unhappy buyers; the sample is the 40 newest English reviews, not a random sample. Never write 'X% of users'. Allowed: '21 of the 40 newest English reviews (8 Sep to 20 Nov 2026)'.

Reviewers name plans that are not on today's grid ('Starter' $20/EUR 20/EUR 24.60; 'Plus' $60 with 2,000 credits; a plan with '400 credits per month' at $20). Either plans changed during Sep-Nov 2026 or regional pricing differs; do not use reviewer prices as current prices.
Company replied publicly to 5 of the 40.

Resolver count rule 2026-11-20: counts are re-derived from the review codes and quotes held in this shard; where the shard text cannot settle a count the lower defensible figure is used and printed as 'at least'. Billing/refund: shard supports 6 (6affc9c5, 6af87ea4, 6aef9a8a, 6aec2ac6, 6ae9d82a, 6ac92883); coder A's live reading adds 6ad0ba33 and 6aa9af70 (8) and a refused refund in 6ac92883 (refused/unanswered 7), but those words are not in the shard, so 6 and 4 stand as 'at least'. Quality/prompt-following: shard supports 6 (6ae14985, 6ade7731, 6ad19745, 6aca6e0c, 6aaae8dd, plus 6ad48d7b whose quoted text 'put things in your video you didn't ask for' is a prompt-following complaint); coder A's broader reading gives 9. Slow rendering: shard 3 (6ac8606c, 6ac1549b, 6a9fe68a); coder A up to 5. Support praise: 4 in the shard codes; coder A's live reading found only 3 name a staff member, so 'named' was dropped. Credits 21 and errors 7 agreed by coder A within range (20+2 borderline, 6+1 borderline); coder B did not re-open Trustpilot (403).
